To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the neuropathology of poliovirus is determined by the distribution of PVR expression in the CNS.
the distribution pattern of the PVR receptor in the CNS is an important determinant of the neuropathogenic potential of poliovirus.
the expression of poliovirus receptors on glial and eependymal cells in the central nervous sytem (CNS) of transgenic mice is important for poliovirus pathogenicity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a tg mouse model for polio and the elucidation of the pathogenesis of poliovirus infection.
the pathogenicity in the central nervous systems (CNS) of poliovirus infection and the role of the PVR in the pathogenesis.
the development of tg mouse models for the study of poliovirus neuropathogenesis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the PVR molecule expressed under the transcription control of the CAG promoter is not sufficient for poliovirus to infect the neurons in the brain and brainstem and induce the clinical and pathological changes observed in poliomyelitic disease.

the PVR molecule plays an important role as a cellular receptor for poliovirus infection, but the distribution of the PVR expression is critical for the pathogenicity and neuropathogenesis of poliovirus.
PVR expression is a critical determinant for the development of paralytic disease after poliovirus infection.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

poliovirus is a highly neurovirulent and neuroinvasive virus that causes poliomyelities in PVR-expressing neurons in the CNS, and that PVR expression in glial and/or ependymal cell in the CNS is not essential to cause the paralytic disease, but it is important for poliovirus to invade the CNS.

the expression of Pvr in the CNS is a critical factor in determining poliovirus neuropathogenicity, and that Pvr expression is not only restricted to neurons in the CNS, but is also found in glial cells and ependyma.
the PVR expression in the CNS determines the tropism of poliovirus infection in the CNS, and the tropism of PVR expression is the most critical factor for poliomyelitic disease.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the distribution pattern of PVR expression in the brain is critical for the pathogenicity.

the PVR molecule plays an important role in determining the susceptibility to polioviral infection of the cells in the CNS and that the distribution pattern of PVR expression in the CNS is a key factor for determining the neuropathogenic properties of poliovirus.
PVR expression is not sufficient for poliovirus neuropathogenesis.
